principle: Count only RF that are absent from the current public pack and whose inland use is supported by a current or authoritative official source. Shared maritime/inland RF are not duplicated.

frequency_reference.source: ANFR CRR fluvial / international VHF channel plan
frequency_reference.paired_rx_note: For a verified boat-to-shore/lock duplex assignment, retain both RF sides. For a boat-to-boat use, retain only the boat-side RF unless a second side is independently required.

results.evidence: ANFR inland boat-to-boat plan plus CCNR 2026 Rhine/Moselle assignments for channels 11/19/20/22.
Current Seine-Yonne rules require permanent channel-10 watch in Paris and Val-de-Marne; Vives-Eaux PCC confirms lock VHF call channels but the article does not publish their channel numbers.
results.rule: Do not guess the lock channels; keep them pending until an official numbered assignment is obtained.

results.evidence: VNF 2026 Saône guide: channel 10 boat-to-boat, channel 12 safety multidiffusion, locks Seurre/Ormes channel 22 and Ecuelles channel 20. VNF 2026 Centre-Bourgogne guide also uses channel 69 on the Yonne sector from Saint-Aubin to Cannes-Ecluse.
results.excluded_from_bfc_delta: Channel 18 is the Lyon crossing assignment and belongs to Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, not the BFC territorial part of the Saône.

results.evidence: VNF Rhône/Saône documents: channel 10 boat-to-boat, channel 18 in the Lyon/Pierre-Bénite sector, channel 12 at Port Édouard Herriot/safety, and lock channels 19/20/22. Channel 18 is counted only on its boat-side RF for the boat-to-boat sector.

Current VNF material confirms active navigation and automated/telecommanded locks on Briare/Loing/latéral à la Loire, but this pass did not establish a numbered VHF assignment inside Centre-Val de Loire. Phone/remote-control operation must not be converted into guessed RF.
Basse-Seine rules use channel 10; the public coastal pack already contains the full national VHF RX dataset.
Current Bretagne navigation information uses channel 13 at the Rance barrage; the 2024 navigation guide also gives channel 14 for Le Châtelier. Both RF are already in the full marine block.

VNF plan effective 2026-07-28 uses five channels 18, 19, 20, 22 and 82 for large-gauge locks. The public coastal pack already contains the full national VHF RX dataset, including both sides of these duplex channels.
Loire navigation requires/encourages channel-10 watch depending on vessel category; channel 10 is already present in the coastal pack's full VHF block.
VNF Garonne/Bordeaux guidance requires VHF channel 12 when entering the Grand Port Maritime de Bordeaux; channel 12 is already present in the coastal pack's full VHF block.
VNF Canal du Rhône à Sète guidance uses channel 10; relevant VHF RF are already present in the coastal pack's full VHF block.
Lower Rhône/Barcarin/Port-Saint-Louis uses channels 10/12/18/19/20/22 and maritime 16 in the maritime zone; all are already present in the coastal pack's full VHF block.
No separate significant inland-navigation network requiring an additional fluvial VHF block was identified in this audit.
Lacustrine radio requirements are outside the metropolitan fluvial rollout and remain a separate territorial review.
